name: Kyungki Kim
title: Assistant Professor
department: Durham School of Architectural Engineering and Construction (Omaha campus)
fitReason: Applied embodied-AI and assistive-robotics fit, especially VLM grounding, tool-call reliability, task verification and evaluation. His physical health-attendant prototype offers a concrete research direction, but a short external-master project and summer 2027 capacity are not advertised.

physicalEvidence.summary: A July 2026 author-uploaded preprint reports a real TIAGo Pro in one unoccupied patient room. VLM agents select shared MCP tools for navigation, manipulation and perception; fixed Cosmos Reason2 grounding and SAM2 support object localization, while lower-level motions are largely scripted. GPT-5.4-mini and two Qwen3.5 models are compared across five task types. Object delivery executes roughly 20 tool calls including navigation, grasping and delivery, with 10 trials per model; the reported completions are 9/10, 10/10 and 6/10 for the GPT mini, 122B Qwen and 35B Qwen variants. Skipped actions sometimes produce false success reports. Room locations and task phases are prepared in advance, no patients or clinical staff participate, and clinical effectiveness is untested. This is a preliminary architecture evaluation, not a new learned motor policy. The May 2026 Applied Sciences article is a separate Isaac Sim study and is not counted as physical hardware evidence.
